bus_apply_consult_p: The briefing will also include a consultation session where you can raise questions or worries about using the bus.
bus_apply_deadline_note: The form must be returned whether or not you want to use the bus.
bus_apply_meeting_p: Those who want a seat are asked to attend the briefing, where the stops, the timetable and the “School Bus Use Guidelines” will be handed out and explained.
bus_apply_return_p: The form must be returned even if you do not want a seat. Without it the city cannot tell whether you want one.
bus_apply_send_p: The city has posted the application form and a briefing invitation to the guardians of children living inside the service area. If nothing has arrived, contact the Education General Affairs Division.
bus_apply_source: Source: Komaki City Board of Education, Education General Affairs Division, “Shinooka School Reorganisation News” vol.6 (August 2026)
bus_area_criteria_p:
Children with a one-way commute of 2 km or more, and areas where local conditions such as significant elevation changes apply, are eligible.
Note: For Shiroyama 3rd & 4th-chome, if a family opts to change its designated school and the commute then exceeds 2 km, the school bus is NOT available.
bus_area_east_p: Ikenouchi, Hayashi, Noguchi, Oyama, and Okusa districts
bus_area_outside: ※ Children outside the service area may be recommended by the Board of Education to use the bus if they are significantly far from the nearest school walking group and group commuting is extremely difficult.
bus_area_pending: ⚠️ The stops, the timetable and the rules of use are being collected in the “School Bus Use Guidelines”, which will be handed out and explained at the briefing for eligible families. Check the official city page for the latest information.
bus_area_size_source: Source: “Shinooka School Reorganisation News” vol.3. Tokadai Higashi is larger on both counts — its bus zone alone is 15.1 km².
bus_faq_a1: What happens if a child misses the bus will be set out in the “School Bus Use Guidelines”, handed out and explained at the briefing for eligible families.
bus_faq_a2: What happens when a weather warning is issued will be set out in the “School Bus Use Guidelines”. It is expected to follow the school’s own decision on whether to open.
bus_faq_a3: In principle, only students in the service area are eligible. However, if a child is significantly far from the nearest walking group and group commuting is extremely difficult, the Board of Education may recommend bus use (per Q&A from the 5th Community Meeting).
bus_faq_a4: Yes. The city covers all costs because the reorganization increases commute distances for these students. There is no charge for students or families.
bus_faq_a5: The stops and the timetable are to be shown at the briefing for eligible families, together with the “School Bus Use Guidelines”.
bus_faq_a6: In August 2026 the application form and a briefing invitation were posted to guardians of children inside the service area. The deadline is 30 August – 30 September, and the form must be returned whether or not a seat is wanted. See how to apply.

bus_map_alt: Map showing the school bus service area in the Shinooka district: the ring outside the two new schools is covered, the area around them is not.
bus_map_caveat: ⚠️ This is an unofficial, approximate map drawn by this site. It traces the figure in the Komaki Board of Education’s “Shinooka District School Reorganization Newsletter” vol. 6 onto map coordinates. The boundary between Tokadai-Higashi and Tokadai-Nishi (red line) has been placed on the Arai–Okusa prefectural road (route 195) from the northern edge of Ikenouchi and Koga down to just south of Shiroyama 1–2 chome, using the road geometry from OpenStreetMap. Shiroyama 3-chome lies west of that road yet belongs to Tokadai-Higashi, so that short stretch is interpolated by this site from the positions of the chome. The rest of the boundary is still the by-eye trace and is off by up to about 300 m in places. Tokadai-Nishi comes out at 7.77 km² against the city’s published 6.9 km², which shows the outer edges still carry error. Tokadai-Higashi is cut off at the top of the original figure, so about 6.4 km² of its bus area is missing (published figure 15.1 km²). Always check the documents the city sent you to find out whether your home is covered. This map cannot tell you.
bus_map_gmap: See this area on Google Maps →
bus_map_kml_note: Import the KML into Google My Maps (“Create a new map” → “Import”) to see the same area laid over Google’s own map.
bus_map_lead: This site redrew the service-area figure published by the Board of Education onto a map. The area around the two new schools — within walking distance — is not covered; the ring outside it is the school bus service area.
bus_map_legend_line: Red line = boundary of the new school districts (Tokadai Higashi / Tokadai Nishi)
bus_map_legend_walk: Not covered (near the two schools it is walking distance; the outermost white is outside the Shinooka district)
bus_map_osm: Roads, neighbourhood names and facilities come from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL).
bus_operator_lead: Running the school buses is contracted out to a private operator. A selective tender was held and the bids were opened on 1 June 2026.
bus_operator_source: Source: Aichi Electronic Procurement Shared System (goods and services), tender result detail (case no. 2605122321900712170). Newsletter vol.4 likewise records “June 2026 — contract signed with the school bus operator”.
bus_ov_apply_p: Students in the service area register to use the bus. Capacity and group assignments are reviewed each school year.
bus_ov_day_p: Operates on school days. Service is suspended during long vacations but runs on school event days such as sports day and term start days.
bus_ov_fleet_p: About five or six vehicles for the two schools combined: minibuses seating 28 (excluding the driver), roughly 2.1 m wide and 7 m long.
bus_ov_free_p: Free for students. The city covers all costs in consideration of the longer commutes resulting from the reorganization.
bus_ov_trips_p:
Morning: 1 trip (all grades)
Afternoon: up to 3 trips (lower grades / upper grades / after extracurricular activities)
bus_p: School buses will be introduced for elementary school students who will face longer commutes due to the school reorganization starting in FY2027 (April 2027). The city covers all costs — students ride free.
bus_safety_check_p: A system will be introduced to allow parents and schools to confirm in real time that their child has boarded the bus.
bus_safety_guide_p: A trained bus escort, contracted by the operator, will ride with students. Escorts receive pre-service training based on established guidelines.
bus_safety_left_p: A system will be installed to prevent children from being left behind on the bus, ensuring safety after boarding.
bus_stats_intro: These three points form the backbone of the school bus plan. See the sections below for details on service areas, safety measures, and registration.
bus_stops_lead: Stops will be set at community halls and other public land where children can wait and board safely. To keep the buses on time, the city plans to keep the number of stops small.
bus_stops_revising: ⚠️ The stops below are the draft as of newsletter vol.3 and are currently being revised. Vol.4 says buses are being driven along the routes to check how easy boarding is, whether there is room to wait, and the routes themselves, and that a revised draft will be published after the problems are identified. The final stops and timetable will be handed out at the briefing for eligible families.
bus_stops_route_note: Place names are given exactly as written in the city’s material. Italics mark the school where children get off. Some routes have one bus reach the school, then return to another stop and run again.
bus_stops_school_east_p: The east car park. Buses enter by the east gate, turn round inside, and leave by the east gate. In the morning they are to line up nose-to-tail near the entrance (about two at most); in the afternoon, side by side.
bus_stops_school_h: Where buses stop on school grounds
bus_stops_school_west_p: The north car park. Buses would enter by the west gate (not in use today), turn round inside and leave by it — or run one-way from the north gate to the west gate. Both morning and afternoon, they are to stop near the covered walkway or the north entrance.
bus_stops_source: Source: “Shinooka School Reorganisation News” vol.3 and vol.4 (Komaki City Board of Education)
bus_stops_time: 🕗 Buses are expected to reach school between 7:50 and 8:15. Going home, up to three runs are planned: after period 5, after period 6, and after club activities.
bus_tl1_body: Contract signed with the operator. Aoi Kotsu Co., Ltd. won the selective tender.
bus_tl2_body: Applications and the user briefing. Forms were posted to households in the service area; they are accepted 30 Aug – 30 Sep.
bus_tl3_body: Trial rides and app testing. Preparation proceeds step by step while the actual routes and stops are checked.
bus_tl4_body: Pre-commute trial. An exercise to get children used to travelling to the reorganised school.
bus_tl5_body: Full service begins with the first phase. School bus operation starts in the Shinooka district.
